text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet is backing a plan to raise the sum of family allowances, said State Secretary Elemer Kiss. The cabinet also agreed to set a minimum health insurance contribution of HUF 1,800 and not to impose taxes on workplace meal contributions. @
- Agriculture Minister Laszlo Lakos has proposed lifting the ban on corn exports.
- The Japanese hotel chain Inter-Continental has become the owner of a 94.9 per cent stake in Forum Hotel, having paid the $49.4 million purchase price.
- A consortium which is to extend a $200 million loan to the national telecommunications firm Matav will be set up today.
- Managing director of Unicbank Peter Felcsuti indicated after a meeting with leaders of the German concern Raiffeisen yesterday that his company is interested in buying Mezobank. @
- The World Jewish Congress will ask the Foreign Ministry today for a copy of the agreement on assets rights concluded between the Swiss and Hungarian governmentsd in 1973.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn will attend a joint meeting of the presidential board of the Socialist Party and the body of executives of the Free Democrats.

- Lawyer Marta Tocsik, whose HUF 804 million commission received from the State Privatisation and Holding Co. earlier this year resulted in the eponymous scandal of recent weeks, failed to show up at a meeting of a parliamentary commission. @
- Parliament's constitutional committee ruled late Wednesday to set up a sub-committee to investigate deals in which the Young Democrats and Democratic Forum sold their party headquarters in 1992.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Although Germany would be willing to transfer military hardware to Hungary free of charge, the armed forces cannot afford to operate these, said Political Defence Secretary Istvan Fodor after signing an agreement on Hungarian-German military technological cooperation with his German partner Bernd Wilz in Budapest Thursday. @
- Some of the austerity measures attached to former finance minister Lajos Bokros will continue to be lifted gradually next year, said National Bank President Gyorgy Suranyi.
- A conference on Hungarian-South Korean cooperation opens at the Budapest University of Economics today.
- The incomes and expenditures of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. totalled HUF 103.4 billion and HUF 288.9 billion respectively in the first nine months of the year.
- Telephone rates will be raised by less than 20 per cent next year, a senior ministry official said.
VILAGGAZDASAG @

- A World Bank team headed by Michel Noel, head of the bank's credit division, is satisfied with the progress made in launching a reform of the pension system, but is "indulgent" toward the sluggish transformation of the health sector.
- The Supervisory Committee of the National Bank of Hungary (MNB) is continuing its probe into the amendment of a contract, signed by two MNB vice presidents.
NAPI GAZDASAG @
- Cigarette manufacturer Pecsi Dohanygyar will finish this year having sold only 8 billion cigarettes, down from 10.2 billion in 1995, thanks to a lively black market, said PR director Gabor Racz.
- The 1996 revenues of GE Lighting Tungsram will probably exceed the HUF 50 billion taken in last year.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
